newsitem.title: CHINA: Sihanouk meets Hun Sen, warrant out for prince.
newsitem.headline: Sihanouk meets Hun Sen, warrant out for prince.

text.p: Cambodian leader Hun Sen met King Norodom Sihanouk in Beijing on Tuesday in a bid to win the king's stamp of approval for his new government while in Phnom Penh legal moves accelerated to arrest the king's ousted son.
Hun Sen and newly-appointed First Prime Minister Ung Huot met Sihanouk with other Phnom Penh government leaders at the king's tightly-guarded Beijing residence.

A convoy of six cars carrying Cambodian flags swept Hun Sen and his delegation past waiting reporters and into Sihanouk's residence. Five hours later they were whisked away to state guest house where the delegation is staying.

Cambodian embassy officials declined to comment on the meeting, but analysts have said Hun Sen, who ousted the king's son, co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh, in a bloody July takeover, would seek the monarch's political blessing for the new political reality in Cambodia.
But in a clear sign that he strongly disapproved of recent events the king said late last week he was dismayed by what had happened which he likened to a "comedy".
He said Ung Huot, who was last week formally approved as first prime minister with the king's permission but without his approval, was a "puppet" of Hun Sen.
On Monday Sihanouk said he was ready to give up the throne if he could be assured Hun Sen would not criticise him for doing so.

Political anlaysts in Phnom Penh said the offer to abdicate could be seen as a challenge to Hun Sen who has long feared the widely revered king would give up his throne, enter politics and challenge him for power.
Hun Sen, who officially holds the position of second prime minister, Ung Huot, acting head of state Chea Sim and a delegation of government officials arrived in the Chinese capital on Monday.
Sihanouk said earlier that the meeting at his residence would be strictly private. Soon after Hun Sen's takeover Siahnouk said he wanted any negotiations on Cambodia's future to be held in secret.
Sihanouk has been in Beijing for medical treatment since February but has said he will return to Cambodia soon.
In Phnom Penh the director of Phnom Penh's military court said a military prosecutor has issued a warrant for Ranariddh's arrest on charges of weapons smuggling.
"The investigating prosecutor issued a warrant for (the prince's) arrest after parliament voted to suspend his immunity," Ney Thol, the told Reuters.
The Cambodian National Assembly voted last Wednesday to strip Ranariddh of his parliamentary immunity.
Hun Sen called for legal action against Ranariddh for weapons smuggling after an arms shipment was seized at Cambodia's main port in late May.

The prince denied he was trying to smuggle the shipment of arms into the country and pointed out that his name was on the shipping documents. He said he was entitled to import the equipment for the use of his personal security force.
But Hun Sen's security officials said the shipment was labelled "spare parts" which they said showed Ranariddh was trying to import the weapons illicitly.
Ranariddh told reporters at the time he needed arms, including anti-tank weapons, to defend himself because Hun Sen had formidable military might including tanks at his call.
The prince left Cambodia shortly before the coup and has vowed to form a resistance movement in and outside of the country.

Since ousting Ranariddh, Hun Sen has said the prince was free to come back to Cambodia but would have to face court in the weapons case and for illegal negotiations with the outlawed Khmer Rouge guerrilla group.
In Cambodia's remote northwest there was a lull in fighting between government troops under Hun Sen and royalist guerrillas on Tuesday.

Thai military sources on the border said Khmer Rouge guerrillas were helping the embattled royalists to defend their last town, O'Smach on the border with Thailand, against an expected push by Hun Sen's troops.

Cambodia' neighbours in the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) decided to remain engaged in efforts to help restore poltical stabiltiy in Cambodia and would embark on a complex and far-reaching mediation effort by paving the way for acceptable elections, sources close to the decision said in Singapore on Tuesday.
